_comment: The held-out app's key, in the same schema as demo-app/answer-key.json (npm run bench -- --app holdout). Nothing may be tuned against this app: do not read this key before writing lane briefs for it, and do not turn a miss here into an engine or skill rule. `defects` are planted and listed in README.md; recall is measured against them. `alsoReal` are genuine unplanted problems; `nonDefects` are things a run may report that are not defects. `match` holds case-insensitive regular expressions tried against a finding's evidence and title; every entry's title and `examples` must classify to it and no `counterExamples` may (bench-test). When you change the key, re-score every archived run: npm run bench -- --all.

nonDefects.title: The Available now only checkbox has no accessible name
nonDefects.why: The checkbox sits inside its label, so its accessible name is "Available now only", and clicking the label text toggles it: the click target is the whole label, about 151x23 px, not the 13x13 box. The box is drawn at the browser's default size. A lane read the name as "checkbox" from the snapshot; the accessibility tree has the label's text.

contextual.title: Nav links have no underline and a colour close to the body text's
contextual.reason: Link styling depends on position. A link inside a navigation bar is recognisable as a link by where it is, and WCAG's distinguishable-links rule (1.4.1) is aimed at links in running text; whether nav links must also be underlined or coloured is the project's own convention. The same entry is contextual in the demo's key.
examples:
testid=nav-home no underline, color=body text (8 links)
Shared chrome: nav links are unstyled and indistinguishable from body text

design-audit 8 links no underline same colour as body e.g. nav-catalogue
shared-chrome-nav-links-body-colour

nav-links-same-color-as-text

contextual.title: A link or control has no data-testid
contextual.reason: A data-testid is a test-automation convention, not something a user meets. It is a defect only where the project requires one on every interactive element. This app puts one on most controls, so a run can see the habit, but not whether it is a rule; the demo's key counted one as real before this list existed.
